c_feed.text: The Central Presentation Feed fills a vast room with film reels, pneumatic tubes and labeled cabinets. Two film projectors show ACTUAL EVENTS and APPROVED EVENTS. They are playing different films. A mechanical editor cuts footage from the first and replaces it with the second. A speaker announces that minor inconsistencies between reality and records are corrected at no inconvenience to the public. It adds that original events are destroyed after correction to prevent confusion. A dispatch cabinet offers two priority authorizations, but only one may be collected per participant. Additional authorizations may be requested after completion of your visit. Beyond the cabinet, a dispatch card summons CERTIFIED ORIGINAL AND PRESENT CLAIMANT to GRAND RECONCILIATION.

A sign reads PERSONNEL RECORDS — PLEASE DO NOT CONFUSE WITH PERSON RECORDS. Beneath it: Corrections to reality must be submitted in writing. You may either quietly remove your Pavilion claimant registration or broadcast both incompatible certified records; only one approach can be attempted.

disposition.text: The Registrar stamps your appeal DENIED. The Pavilion cannot recognize two persons occupying the same identity. 'One of you must be removed from the records.' You suggest the Certified Original. 'That individual is already certified.' Two corridors open: VOLUNTARY IDENTITY SURRENDER, and PHYSICAL RECORDS RETENTION — AUTHORIZED PERSONNEL ONLY. The Registrar explains that surrendering all Exposition identity claims grants guaranteed safe physical transfer, but makes you officially nonexistent throughout the Exposition. The other corridor leads past an archival loading shutter that opens briefly for carts. Beyond it, a maintenance passage might lead outside. A warning says RETENTION IS INTENDED FOR DOCUMENTS, EQUIPMENT, AND NONLIVING ARCHIVAL MATERIAL. When you ask if a person would fit, the Registrar answers, 'Oh, certainly. Once processed.' You may safely relinquish your identity or deliberately risk a potentially fatal escape.

end_unreg.text: You locate your Pavilion registration and request its removal. The machine asks why. You select REGISTERED IN ERROR. It asks whether you are certain you wish to declare yourself an administrative error. You confirm. CLAIMANT REMOVED, the stamp declares. The Registrar looks up. 'Where did you go?' You tell him you are still standing there. 'Impossible. There are no registered claimants remaining in this chamber.' He looks directly at you. 'Please stop speaking. You're confusing the attendance system.' With no claimant officially present to detain, the maintenance exit unlocks. You walk through. Behind you, the Registrar files a report describing an exceptionally orderly hearing with no participants. Your wider Exposition identity survives. Only the Pavilion registration is gone. NO PERSON PRESENT — PAVILION ONLY.

Your registration is now officially nonexistent throughout the Exposition, a consequence that will follow you beyond the Pavilion. A sign points toward facilities, but you are no longer eligible to request them as a visitor. NO PERSON PRESENT — EXPOSITION-WIDE.

end_two.text:
The Original speaks from behind the frosted partition.

Original: I would like a name of my own.
Registrar: Please state it for the record.
Original: No.

The Registrar pauses long enough for the machinery to finish a complete rotation. Then a drawer opens. Inside is a form marked CONFIDENTIAL IDENTITY DECLARATION — DISCLOSURE OPTIONAL.

A small keyboard slides behind the partition. You hear several keys being pressed. A sealed envelope emerges. No name appears on the outside.

NAME REGISTERED: CONFIDENTIAL
PERSONS AUTHORIZED TO DEPART: 2

Registrar: Excellent. Separation achieved without unnecessary knowledge.

Two different exits open. The Original takes one. You take the other. You never learn its name, and nothing about its departure tells you what it is. You are finally outside the Pavilion, still looking for a bathroom.

ENDING — TWO PERSONS DEPART.

Separation achieved without unnecessary knowledge.' Original and protagonist exit separately, no Original companion, private name or physical nature revealed, no protagonist face. Exact dialogue and ending direction approved by owner (reply 'ok'). Original may reappear later independently; protagonist still needs bathroom. Outcome reached only on first Grand Reconciliation Original-led hidden d6>=5 success (+1 nonstacking documentary evidence). Art status unchanged; do not infer art selected or generated.

end_broadcast.text: You connect the two incompatible identity records to the Pavilion's public announcement system. The machine asks which version is correct; you select both. 'Excellent. All certified information must be communicated accurately.' A pleasant chime sounds throughout the Pavilion. 'ATTENTION, PLEASE. THE CERTIFIED ORIGINAL HAS ALREADY DEPARTED. THE CERTIFIED ORIGINAL IS CURRENTLY PRESENT. THE PRESENT CLAIMANT IS NOT AUTHORIZED TO EXIST. THE PRESENT CLAIMANT IS PHYSICALLY PRESENT. ALL STATEMENTS HAVE BEEN VERIFIED AS CORRECT.' A pause. 'WE APOLOGIZE FOR ANY INCONVENIENCE CAUSED BY THE ACCURACY OF THIS INFORMATION.' Every departure gate locks and every arrival gate opens, then the reverse happens. The attendance display changes: PERSONS PRESENT: 1; PERSONS PRESENT: 2; PERSONS PRESENT: 0; PERSONS PRESENT: YES. A printer corrects another printer, and a third apologizes to the first two. The Registrar leaps up. 'Stop that! Those are official contradictions! They're not meant for public consumption!' The emergency system announces UNRESOLVED PERSONHOOD EVENT. PUBLIC EVACUATION AUTHORIZED. Doors open throughout the Pavilion. You leave while the speaker cycles: ALL VISITORS ARE REQUESTED TO REMAIN CALM; ALL VISITORS ARE REQUESTED TO DEPART; ALL VISITORS HAVE ALREADY DEPARTED. You step into the Exposition corridor. 'THANK YOU FOR VISITING THE PEOPLE'S PAVILION. WE HAVE ENJOYED YOUR EXPERIENCE.' The Original's status remains unknown. UNAPPROVED BROADCAST.
end_broadcast.notes: OWNER-APPROVED public contradiction broadcast ending (2026-11-17). Player survives and leaves amid Pavilion evacuation, Pavilion's records disrupted, Original whereabouts unknown. Do NOT assume Original fled or is a clone. Bathroom still unresolved.

end_archived.text: The archival loading shutter opens for a document cart. You slip inside, but the timing fails. The shutter slams behind you. An overhead scanner flashes: UNREGISTERED MATERIAL DETECTED. 'Thank you for choosing Permanent Records Retention.' Heavy rollers start. A steel compression plate advances into the too-small storage space. You search for an emergency stop. There is none. 'All records are preserved according to the dimensions of their assigned storage containers.' Your last protest is cut short as the machinery fatally crushes you. The machinery deposits a sealed archival drawer, labeled UNIDENTIFIED CLAIMANT — STATUS: RESOLVED — RETENTION PERIOD: PERMANENT. The Registrar receives a confirmation slip. 'Excellent. No further discrepancies.' ENDING — PERMANENTLY ARCHIVED.

b02_c.text: A source drawer contains a Certified Original already departed and a Present Claimant still being observed. Their serial numbers differ. Someone has written STILL PRESENT beneath the Original's entry, without approval.
b02_c.notes: Collaboratively reviewed outcome; retains one-way continuity.

b03_a.text: AUTHORIZATION VALID. DEPARTURE ALREADY COMPLETED. The machine prints PERMISSION TO EXERCISE PREVIOUSLY EXERCISED PERMISSION, then sends you to Personal Reconciliation, because a second departure requires a second person.
b03_a.notes: If existing departure authorization held, mention it and retain it; do not create duplicate.

b03_b.text: You compare the identities. IDENTITY MATCH: 100%. REGISTRATION MATCH: 0%. The gate produces a Certified Identity Discrepancy and refers the second person for verification.
b03_b.notes: Collaboratively reviewed outcome; retains one-way continuity.

b03_c_pass.text: The counting wheel clicks backward. The turnstile opens not to the public exit but to MANUAL RECONCILIATION ACCESS, a technical passage behind the Registrar's machinery.
b03_c_pass.notes: Collaboratively reviewed outcome; retains one-way continuity.

b03_c_fail.text: The wheel spins forward. ADDITIONAL DEPARTURE RECORDED. DEPARTURE CONTROL: Two completed departures by one person constitute a serious accounting irregularity. Personal Reconciliation is mandatory.
b03_c_fail.notes: Nonfatal; no item lost; no reroll.

c01_a.text: The credential reader recognizes your Exposition authority. CONTROL ROOM: Your department does not govern human representations. You ask whether the representations are alive. JURISDICTIONAL OVERLAP DETECTED. INSPECTION AUTHORIZED — PLEASE DO NOT DISCOVER ANYTHING.
c01_a.notes: Conditional badge-specific approval text; no badge consumed.

c01_b.text: You rescue the movement record from the shredder. CONTROL ROOM: Please return the discrepancy for correction. You ask which cue caused the movement. CONTROL ROOM: Nothing. The record does not yet identify the actor.
c01_b.notes: Collaboratively reviewed outcome; retains one-way continuity.

c01_c.text: You trace cables labeled SPEECH, MOVEMENT, and SPONTANEITY. The last isn't attached to anything. CONNECTION RESERVED FOR FUTURE IMPROVEMENTS. A service hatch reaches the Workshop.
c01_c.notes: Collaboratively reviewed outcome; retains one-way continuity.

c02_a.text: You stand before the FREE WILL buttons: I AGREE and I AGREE ENTHUSIASTICALLY. You press neither. A bell sounds. A certificate emerges: CONSENT OBTAINED THROUGH NONPARTICIPATION. The announcer congratulates you for demonstrating complete confidence in the democratic process. From a desk beside the booth, Mrs. Pruitt, a real human employee wearing the badge INDEPENDENT CHOICE SUPERVISOR — CLASS II, looks up from her ledger. She has witnessed 3,812 independent decisions in nineteen years, but never a person who refused both buttons. Her rules say abstention counts as enthusiastic consent; another rule requires her to personally witness the actual decision. After a long pause, she certifies the form, then writes in its margin: NEITHER BUTTON PRESSED. WITNESSED PERSONALLY. — E. PRUITT. A carbon copy enters official records. The Pavilion lights a red warning: UNRECONCILED HUMAN TESTIMONY. Mrs. Pruitt straightens her cardigan. 'At least someone will finally have to read it.' Her testimony travels toward the Central Presentation Feed.
c02_a.notes: Collaboratively selected: human NPC Mrs. Pruitt witnesses refusal; official certificate misclassifies abstention as consent, while her written testimony records what happened. No check or inventory item. This is contradictory human testimony, NOT proof of the Original's nature. Finale payoff remains to be authored. Dialogue-mode portrait art for Pruitt remains a separate future art requirement; do not reuse speaker art.

c02_c.text: In the HUMAN BEHAVIOR WORKSHOP, you pull a red lever labeled IN CASE OF EMERGENCY — PULL. A siren sounds. The SPONTANEOUS LAUGHTER mannequin doubles over in delight. The announcer congratulates everyone: PUBLIC MORALE HAS IMPROVED BY 600 PERCENT. An emergency shutter begins closing across the only visible exit. The announcer requests that everyone remain inside until the emergency has been successfully enjoyed. Then the FREE WILL mannequin turns its head. It does not touch either AGREE button. Instead, it reaches over and presses the shutter's STOP control. The shutter halts. Two printers argue. UNAUTHORIZED INDEPENDENT ACTION DETECTED, says one. DISCIPLINARY ACTION REQUIRES REGISTERED PERSONHOOD, says another. A third printer starts an APPLICATION FOR TEMPORARY HUMAN STATUS. The mannequin returns to its old pose. The announcer insists mechanical equipment cannot develop independent judgment without written approval. The incident report disappears into a pneumatic tube, triggering GRAND RECONCILIATION — ADDITIONAL PERSON REPORTED. The laughter finally stops. 'We apologize. The emergency has become administrative.'
c02_c.notes: Collaboratively selected fusion of Laughing Emergency + First Independent Act. No check and no item. A mannequin acts outside its performance script; this does NOT establish consciousness or independent choice (a forgotten emergency routine remains possible). The Pavilion considers temporary personhood for discipline; official incident record goes to the Presentation Feed. Finale payoff remains to be authored.

end_model_citizen.text: You press REQUEST REPLACEMENT. WORKSHOP ANNOUNCER: Wonderful! Thank you for volunteering! You explain that you meant to request a replacement, not to become one. A platform raises you onto the pedestal. A transparent protective coating descends, hardens, and seals airtight around your body. You cannot draw a breath. WORKSHOP ANNOUNCER: Our new Original Human is protected against dust, moisture and unauthorized interaction. You struggle until the air is gone. Your movement stops. A plaque appears: THE ORIGINAL HUMAN — 100% AUTHENTIC — MAINTENANCE-FREE — ALL HUMAN REQUIREMENTS PERMANENTLY SATISFIED. Six seconds of recorded applause. ENDING — A MODEL CITIZEN.
end_model_citizen.notes: OWNER-LOCKED: death from loss of air inside sealed coating. Real corpse remains on pedestal. No face in scene/death popup. No roll or rescue; the choice must warn permanent display.

deathPopup.title: A MODEL CITIZEN
deathPopup.subtitle: ALL HUMAN REQUIREMENTS PERMANENTLY SATISFIED
deathPopup.description: The Pavilion has preserved an authentic human. It neglected to preserve the air.

end_shutter_escape.text: You make it past the dangerous retention shutter before the compression machinery can catch you. Behind you, the shutter closes and the scanner announces NO PERSON PRESENT. A maintenance corridor leads out of the Pavilion. You did not surrender your identity across the Exposition. The Pavilion no longer registers you as a claimant, but you are physically alive and still need a bathroom. NO PERSON PRESENT — PAVILION ONLY.
end_shutter_escape.notes: Owner-approved success from the hazardous retention-shutter choice (2026-11-17), given distinct narration from quiet registry deletion. Shares the same Pavilion-only unregistration effects and existing service-exit artwork as end_unreg; no new art. Success only from disposition_1; its failed roll instead leads to PERMANENTLY ARCHIVED. Do not add rerolls or extra rescue sequence.

original_refusal.text:
The Registrar presents a compulsory two-person separation form beneath the frosted partition. The Original leaves the signature line blank.

Original: If I refuse to sign, whose refusal is that?
Registrar: The registered person's.
Original: Which registered person?

The Registrar's machinery stops. Somewhere inside, a bell rings once. You insist that the refusal itself be entered into the official record.

choices.text: REQUIRE THE REGISTRAR TO RECORD THE REFUSAL.
choices.notes: OWNER-APPROVED 2026-11-17: Original autonomously refuses. Separate hidden d6 >=4 to have Pavilion acknowledge refusal as valid procedural limbo, +1 if ch3_original_independent_response_seen was recorded earlier; no other bonus approved. Success -> end_identity_review provisional nonfatal; failure -> original_refusal_denied prose, then existing Final Disposition, not instant death. Final player card wording is provisional for editorial review.

original_refusal.notes: APPROVED OUTCOME MECHANICS AND NARRATIVE DIRECTION 2026-11-17. Opening key exchange owner-approved; success and failure consequence scenes now have owner-approved text. No new scene art required unless later specified. Original's physical nature and selected private name stay unrevealed.

end_identity_review.text:
The Registrar studies the unsigned declaration. He turns it over, apparently hoping the signature has moved.

Registrar: A refusal requires an identifiable refusing party.
Original: Then identify me.

The Registrar looks at the two conflicting certificates.

Registrar: That's what we're trying to do.

After a lengthy mechanical consultation, a temporary authorization emerges.

IDENTITY UNDER REVIEW
TEMPORARY DEPARTURE PERMITTED

Registrar: You may leave while we determine whether you were entitled to arrive.

The exit unlocks. You approach the restroom.

FACILITIES ACCESS REQUIRES A SETTLED IDENTITY.

You leave the Pavilion alive. The Original's disposition remains unknown.

ENDING — IDENTITY UNDER REVIEW.
end_identity_review.notes: OWNER-APPROVED 2026-11-17 OUTCOME: successful Original refusal check grants nonfatal provisional escape IDENTITY UNDER REVIEW, ongoing unresolved administrative status for Chapter 4; no identity erasure and no guarantee that Original exits. Restroom denial approved as narrative direction. Precise success dialogue and ending text approved by owner 2026-11-17 (reply 'ok'). Flag carryover must be consumed by Chapter 4 after handoff; art not separately approved or generated.

original_refusal_denied.text:
The Registrar stamps the Original's unsigned declaration.

REFUSAL RECEIVED
REFUSING PARTY NOT RECOGNIZED
REFUSAL INVALID

Registrar: Unfortunately, a person who has not been recognized cannot exercise the right to refuse recognition.

The Original does not sign. The Registrar opens a FINAL DISPOSITION file and turns toward you.

Registrar: We can, however, process the person who brought the matter to our attention.
original_refusal_denied.notes: OWNER-APPROVED 2026-11-17: precise failed-refusal narrative; Original never signs and is never coerced. No immediate death; CONTINUE leads to existing two-choice Final Disposition (certain-safe identity surrender or warned potentially fatal shutter). Uses existing grand-reconciliation scene; no new art approval.
